===== FILE 20515__1.pdf =====
September 3, 2025 
 
 
 
 
Electronically Submitted 
 
The Honorable Douglas Collins 
Secretary 
Department of Veterans Affairs 
810 Vermont Ave. N.W. 
Washington, D.C. 20420 
 
RE: Comments on Proposed Rule: Reproductive Health Services, 90 FR 36415 (August 4, 
2025),(RIN: 2900-AS31, Docket ID 2025-14687) 
 
Dear Sir or Madam: 
 
The Ethics & Religious Liberty Commission (ERLC) of the Southern Baptist Convention (SBC) 
respectfully submits the following comments in opposition to the Department of Veterans 
Affairs (VA) Interim Final Rule (IFR), “Reproductive Health Services,” 87 FR 55287, RIN: 
2900-AR57, published in the Federal Register on August 4, 2025. 
 
The ERLC is the public policy and ethics entity of the SBC, which has nearly 13 million 
members in over 45,000 churches in the United States. We are charged by the SBC with 
addressing public policy issues such as religious liberty, marriage and family, the sanctity of 
human life, and Christian ethics. 
 
In October 2022, the ERLC filed public comments with the VA in response to an Interim Final 
Rule (IFR) identically titled, "Reproductive Health Services,”1 which drastically expanded 
abortion coverage in the medical benefits package and under CHAMPVA. In these comments, 
the ERLC outlined why the IFR explicitly violated statutory prohibitions on the VA from 
providing abortion services and undermined long-standing taxpayer protections from funding 
abortions. The ERLC welcomes this corrective proposed rule to restore the VA medical benefits 
package and CHAMPVA to respecting the dignity of human life and the consciences’ of 
American taxpayers. 
 
 
1 Ethics and Religious Liberty Commission Comment Opposing the Department of Veterans Affairs 
“Reproductive Health Services” Interim Final Rule, RIN 2900–AR57 (Oct. 11, 2022). 
https://erlc.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/ERLC-VA-letter-10112022.pdf  
 
 

 
 
September 3, 2025 
 
 
 
 
Southern Baptists affirm the inherent dignity, value, and right to life of every person. 
 
Southern Baptists affirm that every person is worthy of protection from the moment life begins 
at conception. We believe abortion denies precious human lives both personhood and 
protection. The Bible is clear that every person is made in the image of God – including the 
preborn – and his knowledge of these precious lives even precedes the creative act of conception 
(Jeremiah 1:5; Psalm 139:13). Every human being, no matter their stage of development, abilities, 
or circumstances of their conception, bears God’s image and has, therefore, been given 
immeasurable value. Thus, abortion, at any stage of development denies the preborn child their 
inherent human rights, given to them by God. 
 
The “Reproductive Health Services” IFR failed to establish sufficient statutory grounding for 
the rulemaking. 
 
In 2022, the Biden Administration promulgated the “Reproductive Health Services” IRF (RIN: 
2900-AR57) to add abortion and abortion counseling under the covered benefits for veterans 
and CHAMPVA beneficiaries as a direct response to the Supreme Court’s ruling in Dobbs v. 
Jackson Women's Health Organization.2 The VA argued this political maneuver was needed to 
address gaps in access to abortion, saying, 
 
After Dobbs, certain States have begun to enforce existing abortion bans and restrictions 
on care, and are proposing and enacting new ones, creating urgent risks to the lives and 
health of pregnant veterans and CHAMPVA beneficiaries in these States… VA is taking 
this action because it has determined that providing access to abortion-related medical 
services is needed to protect the lives and health of veterans.3 
 
However, the IFR failed to provide any instance in which the life and health of veterans is 
threatened by new state abortion laws because no state prevents providing life-saving care to 
women experiencing ectopic pregnancy, miscarriage, or other life-threatening complications. 
This fundamentally undermines the VA’s reliance upon good cause rulemaking as they failed to 
show in both the 2022 IFR and 2024 Final Rule any emergency reason to avoid standard 
notice-and-comment rulemaking. 
 
The 2022 IFR is inconsistent with President Trump’s efforts to eliminate unlawful and 
burdensome federal regulations outlined in Executive Order 14219.4 Under Section 2(a)(iv) and 
4 Executive Order 14219, Directing the Repeal of Unlawful Regulations, 90 Fed. Reg. 15648 (April 9, 2025).  
3 87 Fed. Reg. at 55288. 
2 Dobbs v. Jackson Women’s Health Org., 597 U.S. 215, 302 (2022). 
 

 
 
September 3, 2025 
 
 
 
 
Section 2(a)(iv), agencies are directed to remove regulations that “implicate matters of social, 
political, and economic significance that are not authorized by clear statutory authority.”5 The 
2022 IFR was motivated as a response to the Dobbs decision for political purposes by the VA’s 
own admission, and violated the statutory prohibition preventing the VA from covering 
abortion and abortion counseling.  
 
The 2022 IFR violated statutory prohibitions preventing the VA from providing abortion and 
abortion counseling to beneficiaries. 
 
Section 106(a) of the Veterans Health Care Act of 1992 (VHCA) expressly states, “In furnishing 
hospital care and medical services under chapter 17 of title 38, United States Code, the Secretary 
of Veterans Affairs may provide to women… [g]eneral reproductive health care… but not 
including under this section… abortions.” 6 This is an express statutory prohibition on the VA 
providing abortions in all hospital care and medical services, including under 38 U.S.C. § 1710 
(veterans) and 38 U.S.C. § 1781 (CHAMPVA beneficiaries). 
 
In congruence with the 1992 law, the VA’s former regulations governing its medical benefits 
package effective beginning in 1999 stated that “the ‘medical benefits package’ does not 
include… abortions and abortion counseling.”7 
 
While the Biden Administration claimed the Veteran’s Health Care Eligibility Reform Act of 
1996 “overtook” the 1992 law, in fact, there is no mention of abortion in the 1996 bill and no 
evidence Congress intended to override its 1992 prohibition on abortion.8 In fact, the consistent 
passage of federal appropriations bills including provisions prohibiting taxpayer-funded 
abortion across the federal government suggests Congress had no intention of this at all. 
 
The NPRM notes that “the VA’s authority to provide abortions is, at least, dubious and, at most, 
nonexistent.” A standard reading of the statute reveals it is the latter and that Section 106 
continues to prohibit the VA from providing abortions. 
 
 
8 87 Fed. Reg. at 55288 
7 38 CFR § 17.38(c)(1), 64 Fed. Reg. 54217, Oct. 6, 1999  
6 Section 106(a)(3) of the Veterans Health Care Act of 1992, Public Law 103-585, November 4, 1992, 106 
Stat. 4947), 38 U.S.C. 1710 note 
5 Id. 
 

 
 
September 3, 2025 
 
 
 
 
Abortion is never “needed” or “medically necessary and appropriate.” 
 
Under statutory requirements, the VA medical benefits package may only include services 
“needed to promote, preserve, or restore the health of the individual” as determined by 
appropriate healthcare professionals.9 From its inception in 1999 until 2022, the VA medical 
benefits package prohibited abortion because it is not a “needed” service for beneficiaries. 
 
The ERLC is grateful to see a return to the VA medical benefits package that removes coverage 
for abortion. The “needed” standard requires a medically necessitating condition to determine 
coverage eligibility. Instances of rape and incest, while egregious, sinful, and tragic, do not 
require an abortion for any medical purpose and are therefore not “needed.”Additionally, a 
proper interpretation of the abortion prohibition established in Section 106 recognizes there are 
no statutory exceptions for rape and incest, only life-threatening complications.10 
 
Furthermore, the Biden Administration’s 2022 IFR led to an issue of federal pre-emption over 
state pro-life laws. Since the Dobbs decision restored states’ ability to prohibit abortion, eight 
states have enacted pro-life laws without exceptions for rape and incest, including Alabama, 
Arkansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Oklahoma, South Dakota, Tennessee, and Texas. It is critically 
important to allow states like these to enforce their pro-life laws in totality to protect the lives of 
as many children as possible. 
 
Turning to CHAMPVA, the longstanding policy prior to 2022 only permitted “abortion” in 
situations where medical professionals deemed the life of the mother was endangered.11 The 
2022 IFR amended CHAMPVA’s policy to mirror the medical benefits package and include 
instances of rape and incest. While CHAMPVA benefits are to be provided in “similar manner” 
with “similar limitations” to the Department of Defense’s TRICARE program, which exempts 
instances of rape, incest, and life of the mother, the NPRM acknowledges the VA has never 
interpreted “similar” to mean “identical.”12 It is, therefore, not statutorily required for 
CHAMPVA to cover abortion and abortion counseling in instances of rape and incest, as it is 
under TRICARE. 
 
12 89 Fed. Reg. 15459 
11 38 U.S.C. § 1781 
10 Section 106(a)(3) of the Veterans Health Care Act of 1992, Public Law 103-585, November 4, 1992, 106 
Stat. 4947), 38 U.S.C. 1710 note 
9 38 U.S.C. § 1710. 
 

 
 
September 3, 2025 
 
 
 
 
Given VA must furnish care under CHAMPVA for medical services that are “medically 
necessary and appropriate,”13 there is no reason to expand abortion coverage to instances of 
rape and incest per the 2022 IFR. As previously discussed, abortions in cases of rape and incest 
are never “medically necessary and appropriate,” as they result in the death of a precious 
preborn life that came about through no fault of their own. 
 
In summary, the ERLC is pleased to see the VA return to the law in its medical benefits package 
and CHAMPVA coverage. This NPRM will undoubtedly save the lives of more children at risk 
of death by the hands of abortion industry. We encourage the VA to continue on this path of 
creating health care plans that value life, protect the conscience rights of medical professionals, 
and rightly steward our taxpayer dollars.  
 
Thank you for the opportunity to comment. 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
 
 
 
Miles S. Mullin II, Ph.D 
Acting President 
Ethics & Religious Liberty Commission 
of the Southern Baptist Convention 
 
 
13 38 U.S.C. § 1781
